marks.gloss_en: they were new produce Levi bar Simon had not acquired: bang so they rise, Levi acquires, then he transfers to you by a cloth (= p_peirei_chadtei, p_hachi_kaamar_shmuel)
that was new produce, which Levi bar Simon himself had not acquired

ומה אם מצוה קלה שהיא כאיסר אמרה תורה למען ייטב לך והארכת ימים -- if for a light mitzva, costing an issar, the Torah promises well-being and length of days, how much more for the weighty mitzvot of the Torah
a person may not take the mother with the young, even to purify the metzora
היכן אריכות ימיו של זה? והיכן טובתו של זה? אלא ... בעולם שכולו ארוך ... לעולם שכולו טוב -- one who did both mitzvot with a written reward died on the way back, so the reward cannot be in this world

a father told his son: climb the tower and bring me fledglings; he climbed, sent away the mother and took the young, and on his return fell and died -- where is this one's length of days, and where is his good?
ודלמא לא הוה הכי? -- perhaps it never happened
ודלמא מהרהר בעבירה הוה? -- perhaps he was thinking of a sin, and died for that
a bad thought the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join to the deed
ודלמא מהרהר בעבודה זרה הוה, דכתיב למען תפש את בית ישראל בלבם, ואמר רב אחא בר יעקב: זו מחשבת עבודה זרה -- the thought of idolatry IS punished
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: 'that I may take the house of Israel in their own heart' (Ezek 14:5) -- this is the thought of idolatry
דכתיב: ויאמר שמואל איך אלך ושמע שאול והרגני -- even on a mitzva errand Samuel feared an established danger
והאמר רבי אלעזר: שלוחי מצוה אינן ניזוקים, לא בהליכתן ולא בחזרתן! -- the protection covers the return too (this also overtakes the answer בחזרתם שאני; an answer cannot be attacked, see header)
סולם רעוע הוה, ומקום דקבוע היזקא שאני (= p_sulam_raua, p_kavua_hezeika_shani)
R' Elazar: agents of a mitzva are not harmed on their way there
והאמר רבי אלעזר: שלוחי מצוה אינן ניזוקים! -- an agent of a mitzva is protected, so how did he die? (amoraic-memra contradiction; kind svara under protest, AUTHORING_DECISIONS 12)
בחזרתם שאני -- on their return it is different
this is what he meant: were there reward for mitzvot in this world, it would have availed him and shielded him from coming to such thought and harm; so there is no reward for mitzvot in this world
there is no mitzva in the Torah whose reward is stated beside it on which the resurrection of the dead does not depend
Rav Yosef: had Acher expounded this verse as R' Yaakov, his daughter's son, did, he would not have sinned
